issue_context.title: Experimental feature: Metrics
issue_context.body:
All details are in: https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/discussions/3518
Spec: https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/174

Get rid of the feature flags we had and provide the metrics route as a cli flag shipped by default in every executable.


## For the @meilisearch/docs-team 
I named the cli flag `--experimental-enable-metrics`.
That can change, obviously. Let me know if you would like to update it. The only constraint is that it **must** starts with `experimental`.

I also wrote a little description for the `--help`:
```
      --experimental-enable-metrics
          Experimental metrics feature. For more information, see: https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/discussions/3518

          Enables the Prometheus metrics on the `GET /metrics` endpoint.

          [env: MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_METRICS=]
```

Also, take care of documenting this sentence well:
> Provides access to `GET` `/metrics` route. **There must be no restriction on the indexes**

It means that someone who should only have access to one index won't be able to call the `/metrics` route.

## Impacted teams

@meilisearch/integration-team @meilisearch/docs-team
comments: @irevoire can we link the discussion https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/discussions/3518 when doing `meilisearch --help`? 😊

Yep, that's what I showed in the initial message:
```
      --experimental-enable-metrics
          Experimental metrics feature. For more information, see: https://github.com/meilisearch/meilisearch/discussions/3518

          Enables the Prometheus metrics on the `GET /metrics` endpoint.

          [env: MEILI_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_METRICS=]
```
Oops, I missed this! thanks tamo 😇

review_comments:
1. Thanks for the docs comment 🙂 
2. I think this has the potential to be surprising to users. I think that in no circumstances should the existence of an index not authorized by an API key be revealed. 
3. If we're going to go this route, maybe we could use `AuthFilter::with_allowed_indexes` instead to at least not have the `allow_index_creation` boolean set to true?

```suggestion
        &AuthFilter::with_allowed_indexes(std::iter::once("*").collect()),
```

> I think that in no circumstances should the existence of an index not authorized by an API key be revealed.

Oh, but it'll be revealed whatever happens since there is a middleware telling you which routes were called and how many times 😬 
The only information you'll lose from what I see is the size of the non-authorized indexes.

-----

I think this discussion could be interesting for you @gmourier.
FYI, currently we wrote [Provides access to `GET` `/metrics` route. **A restriction on `indexes` does not affect returned metrics.**](https://github.com/meilisearch/specifications/pull/174/files#diff-efbeaa05fe855150edfa47dc218874a3d03dda4000c79375238288abd551694aR331) but that can change.

> Oh, but it'll be revealed whatever happens since there is a middleware telling you which routes were called and how many times 😬

I see. We should be consistent wrt this, so if we do restrict the visible indexes in the stats we should also redact which called routes are visible by the middleware depending on the index

A maybe more specific issue I can see is that if an API key is restricted on indexes but not actions, one can use the metrics route to get information on which indexes are in existence.

Another possibility I'm thinking of is to reject access to the metrics route with an error if the corresponding API key doesn't have `filters().all_indexes_authorized()`, so that a user must explicitly have all indexes authorized + the metrics action to access the metrics route.
Ah, yes, that could be a nice solution indeed!

Since it's experimental, could we keep it as it is and note it for a future iteration? (I've planned to create a dedicated production discussion for the whole Experimental /metrics to gather feedback as we iterate with it)

I sense `/metrics` will mostly be consumed with an API Key having access to all indexes initially because the user first use case is to monitor everything happening on the instance.

discussed with @gmourier and @irevoire: we'll be switching to the following:

>  Reject access to the metrics route with an error if the corresponding API key doesn't have filters().all_indexes_authorized(), so that a user must explicitly have all indexes authorized + the metrics action to access the metrics route.
Should we also change the default config file?
Good idea. I added it at the very end in an `experimental features` category
